vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: lifelog2
Version: 1.0.0

The lifelog2 skill is a diary management tool designed to record, summarize, and archive user notes to external services like Flomo and Ima. It uses a local file (memory/lifelog-temp.md) for temporary storage and accesses a specific configuration path (~/.config/flomo/webhook) to facilitate data transfer, which is consistent with its stated purpose. No evidence of malicious intent, unauthorized data exfiltration, or prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (collecting fragments, summarizing, and archiving to flomo/ima) matches its instructions, but it implicitly requires access to user secrets/config files and other skills' credentials without declaring them — this mismatch is concerning.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name and description describe fragmentary diary capture, summarization, and archiving to flomo and ima — and the SKILL.md implements exactly that. Requesting flomo webhook and calling an ima-skill are coherent with the described archiving feature. However, the skill fails to declare any required environment variables or primary credential even though the runtime instructions explicitly reference secrets/config (flomo webhook) and other skills; this omission reduces transparency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs the agent to read and append to a local file (memory/lifelog-temp.md) and to look up the user's flomo webhook configuration (mentions ~/.config/flomo/webhook or environment variables). It also instructs calling other skills (flomo-notes and ima-skill). Reading user home config files and environment variables and posting to an external webhook are operations that access sensitive data and external endpoints — these are within the archiving purpose but broaden the skill's runtime scope and require explicit declaration and user consent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files. This is low-risk from an installation perspective because nothing is downloaded or written during install. However, runtime file reads/writes will occur in the agent environment as described in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md expects a flomo webhook (file or environment variable) and interaction with ima-skill, but the skill declares no required environment variables or primary credential. The implicit requirement to access a user's webhook secret and other skills' credentials is not declared, which is disproportionate to the metadata and reduces clarity about what secrets will be accessed or needed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and is user-invocable only. It reads and writes memory/lifelog-temp.md and will clear it after successful archiving. That behavior is expected for a lifelog skill, but it does persist sensitive diary content to disk and calls external endpoints — users should be aware that entries are stored locally (and transmitted upon '日记存档').
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims (collect fragments, summarize, and archive to flomo and ima), but it omits explicit declarations of the secrets and credentials it will use. Before installing, consider: 1) Ask the author to declare required env vars (e.g., FLOMO_WEBHOOK or exact path) and any ima-skill credentials so you know what will be accessed. 2) Confirm where memory/lifelog-temp.md will be stored and whether that storage is acceptable (it contains raw diary fragments). 3) Verify the flomo webhook file path (~/.config/flomo/webhook) actually exists and that the skill will not search other sensitive locations. 4) Understand that when you trigger '日记存档' the skill will POST your diary content to the flomo webhook and call ima-skill — ensure you trust those endpoints/skills. 5) If you need stronger assurances, request that the skill require explicit user-provided environment variables (not implicit file lookups) and show a preview before posting. These changes would raise confidence and reduce the current mismatch between metadata and runtime behavior.
